title: Rust dependencies resolved by Cargo
description: For a Rust project that resolves its dependencies with Cargo: a committed `Cargo.lock`, builds that obey it, RustSec advisories checked on every change, and the sources and licences that dependencies may have. The Cargo FAQ leaves the choice of committing `Cargo.lock` to each package, so the first two rules ask it of a binary or a service, where builds must be repeatable, and a library applies them only if its team decides so. The licence policy itself is the legal owner's decision and stays in `licence-policy`; build provenance and SBOMs stay in `supply-chain`. The rules on advisories, sources and licences name cargo-audit and cargo-deny because RustSec's own page lists cargo-audit for advisories and cargo-deny for advisories, licences and sources; an equivalent tool meets them.

rules.instruction: Commit `Cargo.lock` for every binary and service of the repository, and review its diff whenever a dependency changes, so that builds, bisects and CI runs resolve the same versions.
rules.verification: Check that `git ls-files Cargo.lock` lists the file, that `.gitignore` does not exclude it, and that a change to the dependencies in `Cargo.toml` carries the matching `Cargo.lock` diff.

rules.instruction: Pass `--locked` to the `cargo build`, `cargo test` and `cargo install` commands of CI and release jobs, so that they fail when `Cargo.lock` is missing or would change, instead of resolving new versions silently.
rules.verification: Search the CI and release jobs for `cargo build`, `cargo test` and `cargo install` without `--locked`; on a scratch branch, require a newer dependency in `Cargo.toml` without updating `Cargo.lock` and check that the job fails.

rules.instruction: Run `cargo audit`, the scanner of the RustSec advisory database, or `cargo deny check advisories` on every change and on a schedule, fail the job on a vulnerability, and record each advisory the team ignores by its RUSTSEC ID with the reason.
rules.verification: Run the scanner on the branch and read its report; check that the CI job also runs on a schedule, and that each ignored RUSTSEC ID is listed in `audit.toml` or in the ignore list of the deny configuration, with a reason.

rules.instruction: List the registries and git repositories that dependencies may come from, and make a dependency from anywhere else fail CI: `cargo deny check sources` does it with `unknown-registry` and `unknown-git` set to `deny` in `[sources]`, since both only warn by default.
rules.verification: On a scratch branch, add a dependency from a git repository that is not on the list and check that the sources check fails; read `allow-registry` and `allow-git` and check that each entry has an owner.

rules.instruction: Write the licences that dependencies may carry, taken from the legal owner's policy, as SPDX identifiers in the `allow` list of the dependency checker, and fail CI on a dependency outside it: `cargo deny check licenses` refuses by default any licence not in `allow`.
rules.verification: On a scratch branch, add a dependency whose licence is outside the list and check that the licences check fails; check that each entry of `exceptions` names one crate and has a reason.
